subject.title: [Feature]:  Non-blocking heartbeat execution to prevent message processing delays

question: Should OpenClaw add a separate non-blocking heartbeat execution lane or worker, or keep heartbeats serialized and only mitigate retry, idle, and cost behavior?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but implementing this changes core heartbeat/session execution semantics and requires a durable contract for state, ordering, retries, and tool side effects.

options.title: Design an isolated heartbeat lane
options.body: Define the heartbeat execution contract first, then implement a separate lane or worker with tests and live channel proof that user messages continue flowing during due heartbeat work.

options.title: Limit to targeted mitigations
options.body: Keep heartbeat execution serialized and address active-conversation pain through the narrower retry, idle-timeout, isolatedSession, lightContext, and model-selection issues.

options.title: Decline the core execution change
options.body: Document the current skip-and-retry model as intentional and rely on existing heartbeat controls rather than adding another core execution mode.

recommendation.title: Design an isolated heartbeat lane
recommendation.body: Define the heartbeat execution contract first, then implement a separate lane or worker with tests and live channel proof that user messages continue flowing during due heartbeat work.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest inspected heartbeat runtime history and prior product-review context for this surface.
